This is an interesting suggestion, since previously it would have been a flat no for performance reasons, but unless I'm misunderstanding, networked IK may have changed that.
Reason being that before you were sending the data for each tracked point, and every player then had to calculate the IK for those.
Now with networked IK, we calculate our own IK locally, and then send the data for the entire humanoid rig.
So correct me if I'm wrong, but basically adding new trackers should now only add performance costs to the wearer, rather than to everyone else. Everyone else in the room would just be receiving the completed humanoid IK data, same as normal, at zero extra cost.

The biggest point against this right now would simply be how absurdly niche the direct audience for this is, but only in regard to the effort required to implement it. So unless I'm mistaken there, it entirely depends on how hard it is to add to the game, and what else that dev time would be used on.
Even without networked IK we could have this if an option to "disable extra trackers" was added.
@{5b348634f5643c23501638a1|full_name}: a tracker is just another point for the IK I don't think it affects performance
@{5cf45849afded207c59f43bf|full_name}: That's what my entire comment was talking about. That on the old system it definitely did, but that on the new networked system, it potentially doesn't.
That would be great, also that with the current ik does not harm the performance of the others
